AbstractText.Label: Aims
AbstractText.content: To compare the evaluation of the small bowel inflammation by MEGS and CE-derived quantitative score (the Lewis score(LS).

AbstractText.Label: Methods
AbstractText.content: CD patients in stable clinical remission were prospectively recruited and underwent MRE and CE; fecal calprotectin (FC) levels were obtained. MEGS score was calculated for each SB segment and the entire SB (SBMEGS). SB inflammation on CE was quantified using LS. Cumulative Lewis score (C-LS) was calculated by summation of three tertiles scores.

AbstractText.Label: Results
AbstractText.content: Fifty patients were included. There was a significant correlation of SBMEGS with LS and C-LS (r=0.61 and 0.71, both p=0.001). The correlation with FC was stronger for MEGS then for LS or C-LS (r=0.68 vs r=0.46 vs r=0.53, all p=0.001). The correlation between the proximal LS and MEGS was significant (r= 0.55, p=0.001); median MEGS was significantly different in patients with LS values consistent with mucosal healing, mild and moderate to-severe inflammation.

AbstractText.Label: Conclusions
AbstractText.content: MEGS score provides accurate evaluation of the small bowel and strongly correlates with FC; the main advantage of MEGS is the accurate quantification of proximal small bowel inflammation unavailable for alternative MRE scores.
